title: Seed swap packet labels
brief:
Prepare a short public notice for the Marigold Row Garden Club’s seed swap. It takes place March 14, 10 a.m. to noon, in the Oak Annex community room. Participants can bring commercially packaged or home-saved vegetable and flower seeds. Ask contributors to label each packet with the plant name and the year the seeds were collected or bought. The volunteer table will have envelopes and pencils. Visitors can take up to five packets, including those who arrive without seeds. The notice is for neighborhood boards and should make participation feel straightforward for gardeners with no previous swap experience.

Aim for 70 to 150 words. Return the complete original work directly in your answer. Do not sign or identify yourself. Do not use tools.

**Marigold Row Garden Club Seed Swap**  
**March 14, 10 a.m. to noon**  
**Oak Annex community room**

First seed swap? Come pick out something you’d like to grow. Everyone can take up to five packets, even if you arrive without seeds.

If you have seeds to share, bring commercially packaged or home-saved vegetable or flower seeds. Please label each packet with the plant name and the year you collected or bought the seeds. The volunteer table will have envelopes and pencils so you can pack and label your seeds when you arrive.

## Marigold Row Garden Club Seed Swap

**March 14, 10 a.m. to noon**  
**Oak Annex community room**

Come pick out seeds for your garden! First-time swappers are welcome. You can take home up to five packets, even if you don’t bring any seeds.

If you’d like to share, bring commercially packaged or home-saved vegetable or flower seeds. Please label each packet with the plant name and the year the seeds were collected or bought. Envelopes and pencils will be available at the volunteer table if you need to pack or label your seeds when you arrive.
